glossary.definition: Identity: What the agent is. An agent access key (Agent Registry) or a federated/workload identity (Federated Identity). No identity, no call. Grant: What the agent may reach. Created automatically when you select an Agentic App on a key, or authored as a policy (pacpolicys) for federated identities. Scoped to MCP tools, A2A agents, or LLM providers/models. Guardrail: What screens the agent's traffic. Per-key AI Guard, runtime protection, and the sensor/enforcement layer for discovered agents. Discovery: What agents exist that you don't control. Self-Hosted Agents and AI Platform Agents find them and attach enforcement.
One credential that IS the agent: scopes, allowed models, rate/budget caps, expiry, guardrail and reachable apps hang off the key; sent as a Bearer header, no sign-in, no token exchange.
The resource layer: MCP servers, A2A agents and LLM providers registered behind the agentless gateway. Selecting an app on a key IS the grant — you cannot issue a grant without an app to point at.

A secretless agent identity: a platform-issued JWT (k8s, CI, SPIFFE, PingFederate) with issuer, audience, subject pinning, lifetime cap and required claims — the new display name for NonHumanIdentity (NHI).
Discovery and enforcement for agents in your own infrastructure: a sensor finds shadow agents and attaches allow/deny/step-up policies.
Discovery and control for agents inside third-party AI platforms (Copilot-class), at the boundary where they cross into your estate.

cards.label: Start: the three layers (plus discovery)
cards.description: Three layers, and every "it doesn't work" ticket is a mismatch between two of them. Then, above the layers you control yourself, discovery finds what you didn't onboard.

cards.label: 1. Agent Registry — Agent access keys
cards.description: You are building or onboarding your own agents and want governed access to models, MCP servers, and A2A agents — the default starting point for nearly every agent deployment.

cards.label: 2. Agentic Apps — The resource layer — the doors
cards.description: You are exposing any MCP server, A2A agent, or LLM provider to agents — you cannot issue a grant without an app to point at.

cards.label: 3. Federated Identity — Secretless agents (NonHumanIdentity)
cards.description: The agent already has a platform identity you trust (k8s pod, CI job, PF-issued token), security requires zero static credentials, or you need claim-level binding (which key, which repo, which human delegated). The default for anything Kubernetes- or CI-hosted.

cards.label: 4. Self-Hosted Agents — Discovery & enforcement for your own estate
cards.description: The customer has agents running in their own VMs, containers, or clusters that weren't onboarded through the registry — the "find and control what's already there" motion.

cards.label: 5. AI Platform Agents — Discovery & control for platform-hosted agents
cards.description: The customer has adopted external AI platforms (Copilot-class tools, SaaS agent builders) and wants visibility and control over what those agents do against enterprise resources.

cards.label: Facts and what is UNVERIFIED

stories.title: Agent Registry
stories.say: The place you mint an agent's identity. An access key is one credential that IS the agent: scopes (llm / mcp / a2a), allowed models, RPM/TPM/budget, expiry, guardrail, and reachable apps all hang off the key. The agent sends Authorization: Bearer <key> — no sign-in, no token exchange.

stories.title: Agentic Apps
stories.say: The resource layer — the things agents reach: registered MCP apps (/<app>/mcp), A2A agents (/<app>/a2a/...), and LLM providers fronted by the AI Gateway.

stories.title: Federated Identity
stories.say: An external token issuer an agent authenticates against instead of holding a key: expected iss, mandatory aud bound to a specific door, subject pinning, JWKS URI, max token lifetime, and required claims. The agent presents a platform-issued JWT (Kubernetes service account, GitHub Actions OIDC token, SPIFFE, PingFederate-issued token…); there is no secret to leak, rotate, or accidentally commit.

stories.title: Self-Hosted Agents
stories.say: Discovery and enforcement for agents you run yourself in your own infrastructure. A sensor (Docker or Kubernetes) discovers agent activity in the environment, reports it to Privilege, and enforces policies on it.

stories.title: AI Platform Agents
stories.say: Discovery and control for agents running inside third-party AI platforms (hosted copilots, managed agent runtimes) — workloads whose identity and runtime belong to a platform, not to the customer's infrastructure.
